key_insight: TideCache aims to make hybrid language models more efficient to serve by dynamically sharing GPU memory across different cache types and managing cache placement between GPU and host memory.
problem_solved: Hybrid models combine global-attention and bounded-state layers with different cache requirements. As context length and concurrent requests change, fixed memory allocations can waste scarce GPU capacity.
method: Target CPU–GPU superchips to manage heterogeneous caches across GPU and host memory.
Use a Transparent Cache Pool to redistribute physical memory pages among cache components while preserving fixed virtual addresses.
Incorporate layer-wise streaming, as indicated by the title; the truncated abstract does not describe its implementation or all three system components.
impact: More adaptive cache management could help practitioners use GPU memory more effectively when serving hybrid models under changing workloads. The provided excerpt does not include measured performance gains.

paper_title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming
paper_authors: Jinbin Luo, Xiaozhe Yao, Shang Yang, Zhijian Liu, Song Han
